elephant.spec:
## Problem

`./pfy build` commit recheck fails on every build. A trial hit the 3h timeout.

Root cause from the tmp/br1106 trial: `recheck_sha()` in `scripts/pfy_build_cloud.py` (about line 1708) builds the recheck copy with `git archive`, `tar`, `git init`, and a single `recheck` commit. That repo is not shallow, so history tests that skip only on shallow clones fail on every build. The named tests are `tests/test_docs_hygiene.py` (about line 63), `tests/test_handoff_headless_1105.py` (about line 58), and `tests/test_dogfood2_1031_report.py` (about line 49). The agent is then told to fix failures it did not cause. Each attempt also runs the full suite (about 16 to 21 min) about four times (post-change gate, flake gate, recheck, retries), so 3h runs out.

The checkout this process was started from is never switched, reset, stashed, or committed. Work happens in a detached git worktree. `prepare_worktree` already uses `git worktree add --detach` for the build worktree.

## Required behavior

1. Build the recheck copy with `git worktree add --detach <dest> <sha>` from `self.worktree`'s repo. The copy has real history, stays isolated, uses its own temp dir, and does not inherit hooks. Always run `git worktree remove --force` and prune in `finally`. Keep the existing gate-rewrote, timeout, and interrupted return semantics from `recheck_sha`. Make the three history tests, and any other test that reads git history for a fixed commit, skip when the target commit is missing (`git cat-file -e <sha>^{commit}` fails), not only when a shallow flag is set.

2. On recheck failure, recheck the base SHA too, with the same mechanism. If the base fails the same way (same failing tests, or both fail), stop with a distinct environment-error status in the receipt. An example status string is `recheck-env-failed`. Do not feed that result back to the agent and do not retry.

3. For docs-only diffs, skip the flake gate and overlap/reuse so the full suite runs at most twice per attempt. A docs-only diff means every changed path is `docs/**` or `*.md`, and no path is code, tests, or config.

Behavior tests use real git repos in temp dirs. Do not use tautological mocks.

- Recheck passes on a docs-only diff in a non-shallow repo whose history lacks the commits the history tests reference (a single-commit-like setup).
- A base-also-fails case returns the environment-error status with no retry and no agent re-prompt.
- A docs-only diff runs the suite at most twice. Count gate invocations.
- The recheck worktree is cleaned up on success, on failure, and on exception.

Update `docs/ops/pfy-build-daily.md` briefly. Use ASCII hyphens. Do not use em dashes. Update the CHANGELOG if one is used.

## Files named

- `scripts/pfy_build_cloud.py` (`recheck_sha` about lines 1708-1772; `prepare_worktree` about lines 2136-2170)
- `tests/test_docs_hygiene.py` (history check about lines 62-71)
- `tests/test_handoff_headless_1105.py` (`_shallow`, `test_handoff_cites_the_landed_commits`, about lines 56-64 and 107-112)
- `tests/test_dogfood2_1031_report.py` (`_shallow`, `test_real_tree_matches_receipts_and_trailers`, about lines 47-55 and 88-98)
- `docs/ops/pfy-build-daily.md`
- CHANGELOG, if the repo uses one (path not given)

## Tests named

- Existing: history skip in `tests/test_docs_hygiene.py`; `test_handoff_cites_the_landed_commits` in `tests/test_handoff_headless_1105.py`; `test_real_tree_matches_receipts_and_trailers` in `tests/test_dogfood2_1031_report.py`.
- New behavior (no module or function names given): docs-only recheck passes when referenced history commits are absent; base-also-fails returns the env-error status with no retry and no agent re-prompt; docs-only suite runs at most twice by counting gate invocations; recheck worktree cleanup on success, failure, and exception.
unstated: Exact environment-error status string (ticket only gives an example).
Receipt field name and shape for that status.
How "same failing tests" is compared (names, order, output, or exit code), and what "both fail" means when the failing tests differ.
Where the recheck dest temp dir lives, and its name.
How "no hooks inherited" is enforced (hooksPath, config, or worktree default).
What "prune" runs (`git worktree prune` versus another command) and from which repo.
Which two suite runs remain for a docs-only attempt, and which functions are the flake gate and overlap/reuse.
Which extra tests count as "any other test that reads git history for a fixed commit".
Path of the CHANGELOG if one is used, and whether a missing CHANGELOG means skip.
File and function names for the new behavior tests.
What happens if the base recheck itself times out, is interrupted, or returns gate-rewrote.
Whether a docs-only classification uses paths relative to repo root only, and how untracked versus committed diffs are listed.

findings.finding: Requirement 1 says to run git worktree add --detach from self.worktree into its own temp dir, keep it isolated, and not inherit hooks, but it never fixes the dest path, whether that directory is pre-created, or its mode. The current dest is self.repo/tmp/recheck-<sha>, which sits inside an existing worktree, and git worktree add rejects a nested worktree. prepare_worktree only stays at 0700 because it mkdirs and chmods before add; a bare add on /var/tmp is 0755. Hooks are shared unless something like the old empty core.hooksPath dir is set, and that setup is not specified.

Requirement 2 says to treat the base as the same failure when the failing tests match, or when both fail. Those are different policies: a base that is already red for other tests would either be an environment stop or a real regression sent back to the agent. The gate return only exposes exit, tail, rewritten, timeout, and interrupted, with no rule for which test ids count as the same failure.

On recheck failure does not say whether timeout, interrupted, and gate-rewrote run a second full-suite base recheck. Doing that on timeout spends another 16 to 21 minutes and can still miss the 3h budget this change is meant to fix. Only commit-recheck-failed is clearly a test-failure comparison.

The finally block must always git worktree remove --force and prune, but it does not say to ignore a remove that fails because add never registered the path. A failing remove in finally can replace the timeout, interrupted, or gate-rewrote return that recheck_sha is required to keep. The external hooks directory, if one is still used, is also left out of that cleanup.

Docs-only means every path is docs/** or *.md and no path is code, tests, or config, but config is not defined (for example pyproject, Makefile, or workflow files), and a docs/**/*.py path matches both sides. Flake gate and overlap/reuse are not tied to functions, so which of the four suite runs to drop is left open even though the suite must run at most twice.

recheck-env-failed is only an example. Existing recheck_sha results are exact tokens (timeout, interrupted, gate-rewrote, commit-recheck-failed), so callers cannot branch on a merely distinct environment-error string unless the token is fixed.

The cited recheck path is self.repo/tmp/recheck-<sha>, inside a working tree. git worktree add rejects a destination inside an existing worktree, and the spec never requires the new dest to sit outside the main checkout and outside self.worktree the way prepare_worktree already does. Add then fails for the candidate and for the base SHA, both look the same, and every build stops as recheck-env-failed, so the history-test check this ticket exists to fix never actually runs.

prepare_worktree mkdir's the dest and chmod's it 0700 before git worktree add so a shared temp never keeps a 0755 tree. The recheck requirement uses the same add and does not require that pre-create and mode. With umask 022 the recheck copy is world-readable.

The excerpt keeps hooks off the caller by git init plus a private core.hooksPath on a nested repo. A worktree shares the parent config, so core.hooksPath is inherited. The spec says the copy must not inherit hooks but does not require extensions.worktreeConfig and git config --worktree. A normal git config write changes hooks for every worktree of that repo, including the checkout this runner must not alter, or the recheck runs the caller's hooks.

findings.scope: docs-only gate count vs base recheck
findings.finding: Docs-only attempts must skip the flake gate and overlap/reuse so the full suite runs at most twice, and the behavior test counts gate invocations. A recheck failure must still recheck the base SHA with the same gate. That third full run (about 16 to 21 min) is outside the cap, and the spec does not exempt the base probe from the count.

Same way is defined as the same failing tests, or both fail. Any base failure, including a different test, a timeout, or an interrupted run, becomes recheck-env-failed with no agent re-prompt and no retry. A candidate-only regression is then recorded as an environment error and dropped.

Finally is specified only as git worktree remove --force and prune. If add fails before the path is registered, or remove fails while a gate process still has the directory, prune does not delete the checkout. The excerpt's shutil.rmtree fallback is not required, so a failed or killed recheck can leave the copy on disk.

The excerpt returns None on pass and commit-recheck-failed when the gate does not start or exits non-zero, including the early archive-failed path. The spec only keeps timeout, interrupted, and gate-rewrote, and adds recheck-env-failed, so a head-fails/base-passes recheck can drop the status the agent loop already branches on.

The excerpt points the extract at a fresh empty core.hooksPath so the gate cannot run the caller repo hooks. git worktree add --detach shares the common git dir, so hooks are inherited, and the spec requires no hook inheritance without saying to set an empty hooks path.

Cleanup is shutil.rmtree(..., ignore_errors=True), so a cleanup error cannot replace timeout, interrupted, or gate-rewrote. Always running git worktree remove --force and prune in finally, including when add never happened, can raise and mask those returns.

prepare_worktree mkdir and chmod 0700 before git worktree add so a shared temp never keeps a 0755 tree, then chmods again. The recheck worktree uses the same add and the spec never mentions mode 0700 or that pre-create.
The problem text says this test skips only on a shallow clone. The excerpt skips only when the repo is shallow and git cat-file -e <sha>^{commit} fails; a full clone still runs the checker.
